examples.en: My sister tickled my side.
If you tickle the child, he giggles.
Please don't tickle my nose with a feather.
The breeze gently tickles my face.
The puppy tickled my hand with its paw.
That song gives a feeling that tickles the heart.

explain: 남의 몸을 살살 건드려 간지럽게 한다는 뜻이에요. '간질이다'는 어간이 '간질이'로 끝나서 '간질여요'가 돼요. 바람이나 감정이 부드럽게 건드린다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It means lightly touching someone's body so it feels ticklish. The stem ends in '간질이', which gives '간질여요'. It is also used figuratively for a breeze or a feeling that gently stirs something.

en: to be sunburn; to be scorched; to be blackened

examples.en: After playing at the beach, my face got dark and tanned.
The wall was blackened with soot, so I repainted it.

examples.ko: 여름 내내 밖에서 일하면 피부가 그을어요.
examples.en: If you work outside all summer, your skin gets tanned.
Put on sunscreen so you don't tan too much.

examples.ko: 피부가 쉽게 그을 것 같아서 모자를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wore a hat because my skin seemed likely to tan easily.
I cleaned the pot that had been blackened by smoke.

explain: 햇볕을 받아 피부가 검게 되거나, 불과 연기 때문에 물건이 검게 변하는 것을 말해요. 피부는 일상 대화에서 '타다'라고 더 흔히 말해요. 연기나 불에서 생기는 검은 가루는 '그을음'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes skin darkening from the sun, or things turning black from fire and smoke. For skin, everyday talk more commonly uses '타다'. The black powder from smoke or fire is called '그을음' (soot).

examples.en: The cold wind gave me goose bumps on my arms.
Stop saying such cringey things.

examples.ko: 저 두 사람은 어디서나 손을 잡는 닭살 커플이에요.
examples.en: Those two are a lovey-dovey couple who hold hands everywhere.

examples.ko: 닭살 돋은 팔을 문지르며 겉옷을 입었어요.
examples.en: I rubbed my goose-bumped arms and put on a jacket.

examples.ko: 팔 바깥쪽 피부가 닭살처럼 울퉁불퉁해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The skin on the outside of my arm was bumpy like goose flesh, so I went to the clinic.

examples.ko: 오싹한 노래를 듣고 닭살이 돋아서 소리를 껐어요.
examples.en: A creepy song gave me goose bumps, so I turned off the sound.

explain: 추위나 무서움 때문에 피부가 닭 껍질처럼 오톨도톨해지는 것을 말해요. '소름'과 비슷하게 쓰는데, '닭살'은 연인이 너무 달콤하게 굴거나 오글거리는 말을 할 때도 많이 써요. 보통 '닭살이 돋다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그런 오글거리는 말을 들으니 닭살이 돋아요.
phrases.en: Hearing such a cringey line gives me the creeps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 낯간지럽거나 오글거리는 말이나 행동을 볼 때 쓰는 표현이에요. 연인이 지나치게 달콤하게 굴 때도 장난스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone says or does something so mushy or cringey that it makes your skin crawl. It is also used jokingly about couples being too lovey-dovey.
phrases.en_equiv: It makes my skin crawl; it's so cringey.

explain_en: It refers to skin turning bumpy like chicken skin from cold or fear. It is used much like '소름', but '닭살' is also very common when a couple acts overly sweet or someone says something cringey. It is usually said as '닭살이 돋다'.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤 땅에 새싹이 돋았어요.
examples.en: Sprouts came out of the ground after the rain.
In spring new leaves sprout on every branch.
Goosebumps rose on my arm when the cold wind blew.
It's the age when pimples break out on your face.
Teeth have started to come in on the baby's gums.

examples.ko: 새싹이 돋으면 화분을 햇빛 아래 두세요.
examples.en: When sprouts come out, put the pot in the sunlight.

explain: '돋다'는 새싹, 소름, 여드름, 치아처럼 땅이나 피부 위로 솟아 나오는 것에 써요. '돋아요', '돋는'으로 활용하고 '돋아나다'도 비슷한 뜻이에요. 해가 떠오를 때는 보통 '뜨다'를 쓰고, '돋다'는 '해돋이' 같은 말에서 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I got goosebumps at the last scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서울 때뿐 아니라 감동하거나 놀랐을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only when scared but also when moved or amazed.

explain_en: 돋다 is for things that push up through the ground or skin, such as sprouts, goosebumps, pimples and teeth. It conjugates as 돋아요 and 돋는, and 돋아나다 is similar. For the sun rising people usually say 뜨다, and 돋 only shows up in words like 해돋이 (sunrise).

examples.ko: 아침마다 머리를 빗질하는 데 오 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about five minutes to comb my hair every morning.

examples.ko: 강아지는 매일 빗질을 해 줘야 털이 안 엉켜요.
examples.en: You have to brush a puppy every day so its fur doesn't tangle.

examples.ko: 빗질할 때 머리카락이 너무 많이 빠져요.
examples.en: A lot of hair falls out when I comb it.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 머리에 대충 빗질만 하고 나왔어요.
examples.en: I just roughly combed my sweaty hair and came out.

examples.ko: 먼저 엉킨 끝부분부터 빗질하면 덜 아파요.
examples.en: If you start combing from the tangled ends first, it hurts less.

examples.ko: 빗질이 서툰 아빠가 딸의 머리를 묶어 줬어요.
examples.en: The dad, who is clumsy at combing, tied his daughter's hair.

explain: 사람 머리뿐 아니라 강아지나 고양이 털을 빗겨 줄 때도 써요. 보통 '빗질하다'로 쓰고, '머리를 빗다'는 동작 자체를, '빗질'은 빗는 일을 이름 붙여 말하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used not only for human hair but also for brushing a dog's or cat's fur. It is usually used as '빗질하다', and while '머리를 빗다' simply states the action, '빗질' names the act of combing as a task.

examples.en: When it's about to rain, my joints ache.
My grandmother, who worked for many years, has thickened joints.

examples.ko: 일이 끝난 뒤 아픈 뼈마디를 주물렀어요.
examples.en: After work, I rubbed my aching joints.

examples.ko: 온몸 뼈마디마다 아파서 감기인 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: Every joint in my body ached, so I thought it was a cold.

examples.ko: 손가락 뼈마디에서 소리가 나서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: My finger joints make a noise, and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 힘든 이사를 마치자 뼈마디 하나하나가 뻐근했어요.
examples.en: After the exhausting move, every single joint felt stiff.

explain: 뼈와 뼈가 이어지는 마디 부분이에요. '관절'보다 구어적이고 몸이 힘든 느낌이 담겨서 '뼈마디가 쑤시다, 뼈마디가 시리다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the knuckle-like part where bones connect. It is more colloquial than '관절' and carries a feeling of bodily hardship, as in '뼈마디가 쑤시다' (joints ache) and '뼈마디가 시리다' (joints feel cold and sore).

examples.en: The baby's breathing seems calm.
On winter mornings your breath looks white.
In the quiet room, only his breathing could be heard.
I felt a soft breath like a spring breeze.
She steadied her breath and began to sing.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 집에는 역사의 숨결이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The breath of history remains in this old house.

explain: '숨결'은 숨을 쉬는 모양이나 느낌이에요. 일상에서 숨 쉬는 것 자체는 '숨'이라고 하고, '숨결'은 글이나 노래에서 부드럽게 표현할 때 더 많이 써요. '역사의 숨결'처럼 어떤 분위기가 느껴진다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: 숨결 is how breathing looks or feels. Everyday breathing itself is just 숨, while 숨결 is used more in writing and songs for a soft feeling. It can also mean a sense of atmosphere, as in 역사의 숨결.

examples.en: Silver hair suits my grandmother so nicely.

examples.ko: 은발의 신사가 지하철에서 자리를 양보해 줬어요.
examples.en: A silver-haired gentleman gave me his seat on the subway.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 머리를 은발로 염색해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That actor dyed his hair silver and became a hot topic.
Before I knew it, my father's hair had turned silver.

examples.ko: 은발 머리를 길게 묶은 할아버지가 지나갔어요.
examples.en: An old man with long silver hair tied back walked by.

examples.ko: 은발이 잘 어울리는 사람은 생각보다 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people look good in silver hair.

explain: 흰머리를 멋있고 곱게 말하고 싶을 때 '은발'을 써요. 그냥 나이 들어 센 머리는 '흰머리'라고 하고, '백발'도 비슷하게 써요. 젊은 사람이 일부러 염색한 머리에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use '은발' when you want to describe white or grey hair in a nice, elegant way. Plain aged hair is usually called '흰머리', and '백발' is similar. It can also be used for hair that a young person dyed silver on purpose.

examples.en: My younger sibling talked in their sleep last night and startled me.
My husband sometimes talks loudly in his sleep.
I have a habit of talking in my sleep when tired.
That friend talked in his sleep at camp last night.

examples.ko: 잠꼬대할 때 무슨 말을 하는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I am curious what I say when I talk in my sleep.
It was cute to see the child talking in her sleep while smiling.

explain: '잠꼬대'는 명사이고 '잠꼬대하다'가 그 행동이에요. 깨어 있을 때 앞뒤가 안 맞는 말을 하면 '잠꼬대 같은 소리'라고 놀리듯 말해요. 이때는 '무슨 잠꼬대야?'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 지금 무슨 잠꼬대 같은 소리를 하는 거예요?
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨어 있는데도 말이 앞뒤가 안 맞거나 엉뚱할 때 핀잔주듯이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to scold or tease someone who is talking nonsense while awake.

explain_en: 잠꼬대 is the noun, and 잠꼬대하다 is the action. When someone talks nonsense while awake, Koreans tease with 잠꼬대 같은 소리. You can also say 무슨 잠꼬대야? in that case.

examples.en: I get scared just by looking at an injection needle.
It stings when the needle goes into my arm.

examples.ko: 새 주삿바늘은 한 번만 쓰고 버려요.
examples.en: A new needle is used once and thrown away.
The child burst into tears because of the needle.
The nurse carefully took out the needle.
Be careful not to get pricked by the needle.

explain: '주사'와 '바늘' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '주삿바늘'이라고 써요. 주사를 맞을 때 몸에 들어가는 가는 바늘 부분을 말해요.
explain_en: A linking 'ㅅ' (사이시옷) is added between '주사' and '바늘', so it is written '주삿바늘'. It refers to the thin needle part that goes into the body during an injection.

examples.ko: 봄만 되면 춘곤증 때문에 낮에 졸려요.
examples.en: Every spring I get sleepy during the day because of spring fatigue.

examples.ko: 춘곤증이 와서 오후 내내 하품이 나요.
examples.en: Spring fatigue has hit me, and I yawn all afternoon.
They say light exercise is good for beating spring fatigue.
They say spring fatigue gradually gets better as the weather warms up.
I keep feeling tired lately, maybe because of spring fatigue.

examples.ko: 저는 춘곤증에 커피보다 산책이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For spring fatigue, a walk helps me more than coffee.

explain: 봄이 되면 나른하고 졸린 느낌이 드는 증상이에요. 봄 날씨 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 점심 먹은 뒤에 졸린 것은 '식곤증'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's the sluggish, sleepy feeling people get when spring arrives, and it comes up often in talk about spring weather. The sleepiness after lunch is called '식곤증'.

examples.en: I've been coughing all day because of my cold.
If you keep coughing, please go see a doctor.
The person next to me kept coughing, so I was worried.
Why are you coughing so much since this morning?
I could hear the child coughing all night.
Many people are wearing masks and coughing.

explain: '기침하다'는 그냥 기침을 한다는 말이고, '콜록거리다'는 기침 소리가 계속 나는 모습을 생생하게 말할 때 써요. 주로 감기에 걸렸을 때 들어요. '콜록거리다' 말고 '콜록콜록하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '기침하다' simply says someone coughs, while '콜록거리다' vividly describes the sound of repeated coughing. It is mostly used when someone has a cold. People also say '콜록콜록하다'.

examples.en: The man grew a stylish mustache.

examples.ko: 아빠가 콧수염을 깎고 나니 젊어 보여요.
examples.en: Dad looks younger after shaving off his mustache.
The grandfather with a mustache is smiling.
The villain in the cartoon has a long mustache.
A mustache has to be trimmed every morning.
I got a milk mustache after drinking milk.

explain: 코 아래에 난 수염이에요. 턱에 난 수염은 '턱수염', 뺨 쪽은 '구레나룻'이라고 불러서 위치마다 이름이 달라요. '코'에 'ㅅ'이 붙어 '콧'이 되는 소리 변화도 눈여겨보세요.
explain_en: Hair growing under the nose. Chin hair is 턱수염 and sideburns are 구레나룻, so each place has its own name. Note the sound change where 코 gets an added ㅅ to become 콧.

examples.en: The baby's cheeks have filled out chubbily.

examples.ko: 강아지가 밥을 잘 먹어서 포동포동 살쪘어요.
examples.en: The puppy eats well and has gotten plump.
I met a cute child with chubby little hands.

examples.ko: 고양이 발이 포동포동해서 자꾸 만지고 싶어요.
examples.en: The cat's paws are so chubby that I keep wanting to touch them.

examples.ko: 포동포동 살이 오른 팔뚝이 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: Those plump little arms are really adorable.

examples.ko: 병원에서 아기가 포동포동 잘 크고 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: At the clinic, they said the baby is growing nicely and plump.

explain: 아기나 작은 동물처럼 살이 보드랍게 올라 귀엽게 통통한 모습이에요. 어른에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니, 주로 아기, 강아지, 고양이에게 써요. '통통'보다 더 부드럽고 귀여운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes soft, cute plumpness, as on babies and small animals. Using it for adults can be rude, so it is mostly for babies, puppies and kittens. It feels softer and cuter than '통통'.

en: to clear one's throat; to hem

examples.en: Grandfather cleared his throat in front of the door and came in.

examples.ko: 말을 꺼내기 어려워서 몇 번 헛기침했어요.
examples.en: It was hard to bring it up, so I cleared my throat a few times.
When I'm embarrassed, I clear my throat without realizing it.
Why do you keep clearing your throat?
Someone in the back row cleared their throat on purpose.
He cleared his throat and changed the subject.

explain: '기침하다'는 몸이 아파서 하는 기침이고, '헛기침하다'는 신호를 보내거나 어색함을 감추려고 일부러 하는 기침이에요. 명사 '헛기침'과 같이 '헛기침을 하다'로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '기침하다' is coughing because of illness, while '헛기침하다' is a deliberate cough to send a signal or hide awkwardness. People also say '헛기침을 하다' with the noun.
